extracted.intended_audience: typographers, printers, book and type designers, press production staff
extracted.subtask_description: A printed/type specimen catalog showing fonts in use at multiple point sizes and styles, intended to let designers and printers evaluate face characteristics, legibility, and suitability for book production. Samples include body-text paragraphs, display lines, multilingual scripts, special characters, and notes on leaded vs. solid setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show font name and point size
rubrics_metrics.description: Each specimen is labeled with the face name and its point size (e.g., 'CASLON OLD STYLE — EIGHT POINT', 'LINOTYPE — NINE POINT NO. ONE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label each sample with the typeface and the exact point size to allow direct comparison across faces and sizes; the page repeatedly presents headings like 'LINOTYPE NINE POINT NO. ONE', 'CASLON OLD STYLE TEN POINT', etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present body-text sample for legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a continuous paragraph of representative text set in the face and size (the page repeatedly uses the same paragraph about Polybius/Carthage to show body text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a standard, reasonably long paragraph to reveal letterspacing, word spacing, hyphenation behavior, and overall texture at each size; the specimen uses the same running paragraph across sizes for consistent comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include display/capitals lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide uppercase display lines (e.g., 'THE FIRST TIME THAT THE GRAND PROSPECT HAD BEEN HELD FORTH') in various display sizes to show headline/different-weight appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show large-capital lines and display text at multiple sizes so designers can judge weight, spacing, and impact separate from body text; the catalog shows display lines at 18, 22, 24, 30, 36, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show multiple point sizes (range)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens must show the face at many point sizes (examples on the page range from six point up to 48+ point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide samples at small text sizes (6–10 pt), standard text sizes (10–12 pt), and display sizes (14–48+ pt) so users can evaluate performance across intended uses; the book lists numerous sizes (six, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, fourteen, eighteen, twenty-two, twenty-four, thirty, thirty-six, forty-eight, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate setting method: leaded vs. solid
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens explicitly mark samples as '[Leaded]' or '[Solid]' to show the effect of added leading versus solid setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both leaded and solid versions where relevant so readers can see vertical spacing effects on texture and readability; many samples on the page are annotated '[Leaded]' or '[Solid]'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show style variants (italic, bold, condensed, extended, bold/italic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the face's stylistic variants such as italic, italic small sizes, condensed, extended, bold, and bold-italic (e.g., 'CASLON OLD STYLE ITALIC', 'CONDENSED OLD STYLE', 'EXTENDED OLD STYLE', 'CHELTENHAM BOLD').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display each available style so designers can assess harmony across weights and uses (body, emphasis, display); the specimen book dedicates sections to italic, condensed, extended, and bold variants at multiple sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multilingual/script samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide samples in multiple scripts and languages (the page includes Greek, Antique Greek, Inscription Greek, Hebrew, Nestorian Syriac, Arabic, Ethiopic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the face handles diacritics, glyph shapes, and proportions across scripts so users can judge suitability for multilingual publishing; specimens include labeled sections like 'PORSON GREEK', 'ANTIQUE GREEK', 'HEBREW', 'ARABIC', etc., at various point sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show special characters, accented letters, and diacritics
rubrics_metrics.description: Include dedicated lines/blocks demonstrating accented letters and special characters (e.g., 'ACCENTED LETTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT', 'SPECIAL CHARACTERS — ALL SIZES', 'MISCELLANEOUS SIGNS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive accented characters and punctuation to confirm glyph coverage and spacing; the specimen lists accented letters and symbol blocks in several sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show numerals and glyph variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Display numerals (e.g., '1234567890') and alternative ornamentation/punctuation to observe numeral spacing and appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include lining/old-style numerals, tabular/non-tabular variants, and repeated numeral strings so users can assess numeric color and alignment; the page repeatedly embeds '1234567890' within samples and decorative numeral runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show small-size performance (tiny point samples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide very small-size specimens (e.g., six-, seven-, eight-point) including condensed or display variants to assess legibility at minute sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include text at the smallest intended sizes with attention to clarity of counters and stroke contrast; the catalog includes six- and eight-point samples (e.g., 'BOOKMAN OLD STYLE — SIX POINT', 'CHELTENHAM WIDE — SIX POINT').

rubrics_metrics.name: Group specimens by foundry/setting method for comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Label and group samples by the typecasting/setting system or foundry (e.g., 'LINOTYPE', 'MONOTYPE', 'UNOTYPE', 'THE UNIVERSITY OF CHICAGO PRESS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize pages so users can compare the same face across casting/setting systems and see differences due to technology or supplier; the page groups blocks under headings such as 'LINOTYPE', 'MONOTYPE', 'UNOTYPE'.
